portfolio.week_narrative: A brutal week for growth stocks as rising Treasury yields dominated every session. The 30-year Treasury yield cracked 5% for the first time in nearly two decades, the 20-year hit 5.19%, and the 10-year approached 4.66% — all at 52-week highs. The catalyst: Kevin Warsh was sworn in as the new Fed Chair, and markets quickly realized his path to rate cuts is far harder than Trump expected. Nasdaq led the decline at -2.01% as high-duration tech names got hammered by the rate spike. The one bright spot: MSFT surged 3% after Bill Ackman's Pershing Square disclosed a new stake, and NFLX quietly recovered +2%.

covered_calls.market_iv_context: VIX elevated above 20 as Treasury yields spike — this is one of the best IV environments for covered call premium collection we have seen this year. Rising rate fear creates persistent choppiness, which is ideal for selling calls. However, NVDA earnings tomorrow mean the most important play of the month happens AFTER the report, not before.
covered_calls.covered_call_primer: A covered call means selling someone the right to buy your shares at a set price by a set date. You collect the premium today regardless of outcome. If the stock stays below the strike price, you keep the shares and the full premium. If it rises above the strike, your shares get called away at that price — you still profit, just capped at the strike.
